plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $30, I should bid exactly $30 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no benefit to shading my bid down, and bidding above my value risks losses if I win at a price above my value. With a value of $7, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $7 to ensure I only win when profitable and never overpay.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: since the price paid depends only on the second-highest bid (not my own bid, given I win), overbidding risks paying more than my value, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' strategies, I should bid exactly my value of $36 to maximize expected profit.
